id: v-2-access-logs-index
title: "List access logs"
description: "Paginated feed of access events (lock opens/closes, gate activations, unit-access changes) across your locations. Each log carries three timestamps: `effective_at` is the one to sort and display — it equals `happened_at` when the device reported one, falling back to `created_at` (server receipt) for older hardware or offline-uploaded events where `happened_at` is null. Filter by `location`, `unit`, `key` (e.g. `lock.open_successful`), `log_type` (`units` / `entrypoints` / `locks`), and date range (`from` / `to` on `effective_at`). Each log also says who performed it. `performer_type` is `tenant`, `employee` (your staff), `partner_employee` (staff of a partner organization you have given access to your locations), `consumer`, or `kiss_staff` (KISS support or installation staff). `performer_id` is that person's KISS ULID; for an active tenant it is the same value `GET /tenants` returns as `tenant_id`, and a tenant merged into another account is reported as that account. It is null for `kiss_staff` and for an account that no longer exists. `external_tenant_id` is the tenant's id in your system at the location where the event happened. If the tenant holds different ids at different locations, it can differ from the single id `GET /tenants` shows. It is null for anyone who is not a tenant, and for a tenant with no id from your system on file (common for guests and secondary tenants, who are reported as themselves, never as the lease holder). Results are paged (15 per page, `per_page` up to 100) with details in `meta.pagination`. Supports conditional requests via `ETag` / `If-None-Match` with a 60-second cache window. Needs the `read:logs` scope."

Paginated feed of access events (lock opens/closes, gate activations, unit-access changes) across your locations. Each log carries three timestamps: `effective_at` is the one to sort and display — it equals `happened_at` when the device reported one, falling back to `created_at` (server receipt) for older hardware or offline-uploaded events where `happened_at` is null. Filter by `location`, `unit`, `key` (e.g. `lock.open_successful`), `log_type` (`units` / `entrypoints` / `locks`), and date range (`from` / `to` on `effective_at`). Each log also says who performed it. `performer_type` is `tenant`, `employee` (your staff), `partner_employee` (staff of a partner organization you have given access to your locations), `consumer`, or `kiss_staff` (KISS support or installation staff). `performer_id` is that person's KISS ULID; for an active tenant it is the same value `GET /tenants` returns as `tenant_id`, and a tenant merged into another account is reported as that account. It is null for `kiss_staff` and for an account that no longer exists. `external_tenant_id` is the tenant's id in your system at the location where the event happened. If the tenant holds different ids at different locations, it can differ from the single id `GET /tenants` shows. It is null for anyone who is not a tenant, and for a tenant with no id from your system on file (common for guests and secondary tenants, who are reported as themselves, never as the lease holder). Results are paged (15 per page, `per_page` up to 100) with details in `meta.pagination`. Supports conditional requests via `ETag` / `If-None-Match` with a 60-second cache window. Needs the `read:logs` scope.
